one_liner: Lua-scripted C tensor library (TH) behind the Torch7 framework; a 2015-16 Bosch study found it fastest on CPU versus Caffe and Theano.
what_it_does: torch7 is the core package of the Torch7 framework: the TH C library of strided, reference-counted n-d tensors with math, BLAS/LAPACK wrappers, random numbers and serialization, plus luaT bindings that expose it to Lua (LuaJIT 2.1 by default in torch/distro). Neural-network layers live in the separate torch/nn package (THNN), and GPU support in cutorch/cunn. It is a different API from Caffe prototxt models and Theano graphs, so nothing is drop-in; its C backend was forked into PyTorch's ATen, which is where new work went.
how_it_is_fast: Dense work goes to the system BLAS: THBlas gemm/gemv call sgemm_/dgemm_ when CMake finds a BLAS (torch/distro builds OpenBLAS with USE_OPENMP=1), and fall back to naive triple loops otherwise. Elementwise ops use runtime-dispatched SSE/AVX/AVX2/NEON/VSX kernels (THVectorDispatch) and OpenMP loops above TH_OMP_OVERHEAD_THRESHOLD = 100000 elements. Convolution in nn is im2col plus GEMM (THNN SpatialConvolutionMM), and its forward and input-gradient passes run '#pragma omp parallel for' across the images of a batch; Caffe's native convolution loops over images serially and relies on BLAS threads, which is a plausible reason Torch scaled better on the small LeNet GEMMs (an inference, not stated by the study).
when_to_use: Maintaining or reproducing existing Lua Torch7 research code (2014-2017 models, .t7 files) on CPU
Small CPU-bound convnets at batch sizes of tens of images, where batch-level OpenMP over many cores helps and the study's LeNet setting (batch 64, 12 threads) applies
Embedding a compact BSD-licensed C tensor library (lib/TH, C99/gnu99, optional BLAS/LAPACK) where ATen's C++ build is too heavy
Historical baselines: comparing a new kernel against the framework most 2015-era convnet benchmarks used
when_not_to_use: Any new project: the README says 'Torch is not in active development' and that the TH/THNN backend continues as ATen in PyTorch; the community was 'close to non-existent' by 2019

GPU training of larger models: in the study authors' own updated M40/cuDNNv4 table Torch is slowest on AlexNet gradient (408.8 ms vs Neon 247.0 and Caffe 279.3) and on LSTM (93.2 ms vs Theano 17.3); in soumith/convnet-benchmarks its native GPU convolution is slightly slower than Caffe's
Modern platforms: open issues report install failures on Apple M1 (#1240), AArch64 Fedora 33 (#1231), Ubuntu 20.04 under WSL (#1245) and current CUDA/cuDNN combinations
Builds without a tuned BLAS: if CMake does not find one, gemm/gemv fall back to unblocked triple loops and the CPU speed advantage disappears
NumPy-style code: TH has no broadcasting (the README says ATen added it), and Python users have no supported binding

integration.dependencies: Lua 5.1 or LuaJIT (distro default LUAJIT21), luarocks packages paths and cwrap, CMake; optional BLAS (OpenBLAS or MKL), LAPACK and OpenMP; torch/nn for neural-network layers
integration.min_toolchain: C99 (gnu99) compiler, CMake 2.8 (2.8.12 on macOS); GCC 4.6.2+ for OpenMP on macOS per CMakeLists.txt
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS primarily (torch/distro scripts for Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE, Debian, CentOS); Windows via CMake build commands in the rockspec; SIMD paths for x86 SSE/AVX/AVX2, ARM NEON and ppc64le VSX, disableable with TH_NO_AVX2, TH_NO_AVX, TH_NO_SSE, TH_NO_VSX
integration.thread_safety: not documented; ops parallelize internally with OpenMP and torch.setnumthreads sets the process-wide OpenMP thread count (THSetNumThreads calls omp_set_num_threads); tensor refcounts and the heap counter use atomics

gotchas: The measured 'Torch' is torch7 plus torch/nn (THNN) plus whatever BLAS was linked; the convolution kernel credited for the CPU win lives in torch/nn, not in this repository.

Study harness (DL-Benchmarks/DL-Benchmarks, read this session): Torch timing covers model:forward and model:backward only and excludes the ClassNLLCriterion, while Caffe's 'caffe time' includes its DummyData and SoftmaxWithLoss layers and feeds constant input. The Theano LeNet uses the legacy theano.tensor.nnet.conv.conv2d op, and theano/readme.txt gives the CPU command as THEANO_FLAGS='device=cpu' with no floatX=float32, so unless a local .theanorc overrode Theano's float64 default the CPU Theano rows ran in double precision while Torch set torch.FloatTensor (the paper, which might state the setting, was not reachable). Both tilt the comparison toward Torch, the floatX point mainly against Theano; the Torch and Theano scripts ship configured for GPU (conf.mode = 'GPU'; Torch's 12 threads hard-coded).

SpatialConvolutionMM keeps an unfolded im2col buffer for the whole batch (finput is batch x kW*kH*nInputPlane x outH*outW), so memory grows with batch size; accGradParameters runs serially over the batch.
TH memory is invisible to the Lua garbage collector except through THSetGCHandler heap-size heuristics, so Lua code that churns tensors can hold large amounts of memory until a collection runs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Torch7 over PyTorch only to keep legacy Lua Torch code running; PyTorch inherited the same TH kernels through ATen and is maintained. Against Caffe, Torch7 was the faster CPU option in the Bosch study but not on GPU convolution; for a tiny dependency-free C network on CPU, KANN is the smaller choice.
verified_claims_summary: Bahrampour et al. (Robert Bosch, arXiv 1511.06435, ICLR 2016 workshop) timed a modified LeNet at batch 64 on a six-core Hyper-Threading CPU, Torch at 1/6/12 threads against Caffe fixed at 12 threads, Theano at 6/12 and Neon at 1, and concluded Torch was best on CPU (about 4x Caffe's gradient time per v3 search snippets, 16.5 vs 66.4 ms); the per-cell milliseconds, CPU model and BLAS remain unread because arxiv.org is blocked here. The public companion code (DL-Benchmarks, MIT) confirms the network, batch size, 200 warm-up and 200 timed iterations, float32 Torch tensors and 12 Torch threads, but its README publishes only GPU (M40, cuDNNv4) updates, where Torch leads only LeNet forward.
status_note: Stale: the last commits (2025-03-31) merge a typo fix and an arm64-osx build fix, substantive development stopped in 2017 and the README declares it not in active development; BSD-3-Clause and buildable from source, but treat it as a frozen legacy codebase. The study's benchmark code is public (github.com/DL-Benchmarks/DL-Benchmarks, MIT) and its documented Theano CPU command leaves floatX at the float64 default, so the 12x-over-Theano figure is suspect; tier stays C until the paper's CPU table, hardware, BLAS and floatX setting are read.
